provisions.summary: Under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, in the absence of a contract to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for residential/monthly purposes requires at least 15 days notice expiring with the end of a month of tenancy. Abrupt 24-hour or 7-day eviction demands without contractual basis are generally unlawful.

Security deposits paid by tenants are held in trust and must be refunded upon peaceful handover, subject only to reasonable deductions for actual documented unpaid rent or structural damage. Unilateral total forfeiture without receipts or breakdown is a disputable unfair practice.
provisions.citation: Model Tenancy Act / State Rent Control Provisions

provisions.summary: Tenants have a common-law right to peaceful possession and quiet enjoyment. A landlord cannot arbitrarily enter premises at any hour without prior notice; standard legal guidelines mandate at least 24 hours prior written or electronic notice for reasonable inspection.

Under Section 2(46) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, an 'unfair contract' includes terms that cause a significant change in consumer rights, such as requiring excessive security deposits, imposing unreasonable penalties, or unilateral cancellation without notice.

Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns (2023) prohibit any person or platform from engaging in specified dark patterns (drip pricing, subscription traps, basket sneaking). Engaging in such practices amounts to misleading advertisement or unfair trade practice.
provisions.citation: CCPA Dark Pattern Guidelines 2023 read with Section 18 Consumer Protection Act
